signals.score_reason: high-value open-source ecosystem signal; agentic AI relevance. Final score: 66. Freshness: source age 0d.
signals.brief_en:
Title: Tsunami1212/takeferry

A Hermes‑based agent designed for screenwriters to test identical shots across multiple AI video platforms. It integrates the workflow into a LibTV or Pippit canvas via the MCP (Media Control Protocol), enabling rapid iteration and comparative analysis of generated footage. Current capabilities are limited to supported platforms and require manual configuration of prompts and parameters. Further development is needed to automate quality assessment and rights management.

العنوان: Tsunami1212/takeferry

signals.brief_en: Volant Manticore, a cyber‑espionage group linked to Iran, has expanded its operations from Cyprus to Saudi Arabia. According to Industrial Cyber, the group is targeting critical sectors such as energy, petrochemicals, telecommunications and government networks. The campaign uses custom malware and credential‑stealing tools, leveraging phishing and supply‑chain compromises. While attribution to Iranian actors is supported by code similarities and infrastructure overlap, definitive state sponsorship remains unconfirmed. Organizations in the region are advised to strengthen network segmentation, enforce multi‑factor authentication, and monitor for known Indicators of Compromise.

So what comes next? 🔗 Read in full https://t.co/mdfIG3XW7F ⬇️
signals.score_reason: Twitter/X discussion signal; strategic/security relevance. Final score: 62. Freshness: source age 0.36d.
signals.brief_en:
Title: @FLI_org – Autonomous Weapons Newsletter Summary
The military AI governance team reports on last week’s @UNGeneva CCW Review. Despite a majority of states expressing support for an AI weapons treaty, negotiations were not initiated. The impasse highlights the need for continued diplomatic engagement and confidence‑building measures to address emerging autonomous weapon risks.
Key points:
- Broad state support for regulation, but no formal talks launched.
- Immediate focus: develop interim guidelines, share transparency data, and strengthen existing CCW mechanisms.
- Next steps: convene expert working groups, explore confidence‑building measures, and prepare a draft framework for future treaty negotiations.
signals.brief_ar:
العنوان: @FLI_org – ملخص النشرة حول الأسلحة الذاتية
تقرير فريق حوكمة الذكاء الاصطناعي العسكري عن مراجعة مؤتمر @UNGeneva CCW الأسبوع الماضي. رغم أن أغلبية الدول أبدت دعمها لمعاهدة أسلحة الذكاء الاصطناعي، لم تُفتتح أي مفاوضات. يُظهر هذا الجمود الحاجة إلى مواصلة الجهود الدبلوماسية وإجراءات بناء الثقة لمواجهة مخاطر الأسلحة الذاتية.
النقاط الرئيسة:
- دعم واسع للدول بتنظيم الأسلحة، لكن لا محادثات رسمية بدأت.
- التركيز الفوري: وضع إرشادات مؤقتة، تبادل بيانات الشفافية، وتعزيز آليات CCW الحالية.
- الخطوات القادمة: تشكيل مجموعات عمل خبراء، استكشاف إجراءات بناء الثقة، وإعداد مسودة إطار لتفاوض معاهدة مستقبلية.

signals.brief_en: Ukraine’s digitalised warfare relies more on integrated C4ISR systems and centralized data authority than on AI algorithms. The key lesson for the UK and NATO is to prioritize interoperable platforms, robust data governance, and command‑and‑control structures that can fuse sensor inputs and operational data in real time. AI can augment decision‑making, but without a unified architecture and strong authority, its impact remains limited.

signals.title: @piotrkulpinski: Same here: all 12 of my sites run on one Hetzner box (€59/mo, 64 GB RAM). The scary part is the day it dies. Everything goes down at once, a
signals.content: Same here: all 12 of my sites run on one Hetzner box (€59/mo, 64 GB RAM). The scary part is the day it dies. Everything goes down at once, and backups only help if they can rebuild the whole thing. So today I tested it. I rented a fresh server by the hour and rebuilt everything on it from backups only. Production kept running the whole time. 36 minutes later all 12 sites were back up. The server cost €0.11. The test also found 4 things my backups were missing: – a network I'd created by hand on the server – the login my server uses to download app images – a database setting that doesn't end up in database dumps – two apps that connect to the live database while they build Any of these would've turned a 36-minute recovery into a long night of guessing. All fixed now. The server also backs up its own config every night, and I get an alert if that backup stops. If you run everything on one box too: – back up the server's config, not only the databases – do a real restore on a throwaway server and time it Better to find out now than mid-outage 😅
signals.score_reason: Twitter/X discussion signal. Final score: 40. Freshness: source age 0.57d.
signals.brief_en: Brief: A user reports that 12 websites are hosted on a single Hetzner server (64 GB RAM, €59/month). To assess resilience, they rented an hourly server, restored all sites from backups, and achieved full recovery in 36 minutes at a cost of €0.11. The drill revealed four backup gaps: a manually created network, the server login for pulling container images, a database configuration not captured in dumps, and two applications that connect to the live database during build. The test underscores the risk of single‑point failure and the need for comprehensive backup procedures that capture infrastructure and runtime dependencies.
signals.brief_ar: ملخص: يوضح أحد المستخدمين أن 12 موقعًا تستضيفها خادم واحد من Hetzner (64 جيجابايت RAM، €59/شهر). لاختبار القدرة على الاستعادة، استأجر خادمًا بالساعة وأعاد بناء جميع المواقع من النسخ الاحتياطية، وتم استعادة كل شيء خلال 36 دقيقة بتكلفة €0.11. كشف الاختبار أربعة نقص في النسخ الاحتياطية: شبكة تم إنشاؤها يدويًا على الخادم، بيانات تسجيل الدخول التي يستخدمها الخادم لتنزيل صور التطبيقات، إعداد قاعدة بيانات لا يُدرج في تفريغ قاعدة البيانات، وتطبيقان يتصلان بقاعدة البيانات الحية أثناء البناء. يبرز الاختبار خطر الاعتماد على نقطة فشل واحدة وحاجة المؤسسات إلى إجراءات نسخ احتياطي شاملة تشمل البنية التحتية والاعتمادات التشغيلية.
